subject: Urban Planning
title: The Embarcadero Freeway: Earthquake as Urban Planner
description: A 1-minute de-risking session on The Embarcadero Freeway: Earthquake as Urban Planner.

hook.text: San Francisco's Embarcadero Freeway cut the city off from its waterfront for 30 years. Citizens hated it.

buildup.text: Built in 1959, the double-deck highway blocked views, killed businesses, and darkened the streets below.

discovery.text: Voters tried twice to demolish it. Both times, highway supporters and commuters blocked the vote.

twist.text: The 1989 Loma Prieta earthquake damaged it beyond repair. The city had no choice but to tear it down.

climax.text: A palm-lined boulevard replaced it. Property values soared. The waterfront became the city's best feature.

punchline.text: What politics couldn't fix, an earthquake did.

quiz.question: What forced San Francisco to remove the Embarcadero Freeway?
options: A citywide referendum finally passed in 1988
The 1989 Loma Prieta earthquake damaged it beyond repair
Federal highway funding was redirected to transit projects
